2608.31076.title: Learning to Evaluate Before Improving: Automatic Rubric Induction for Automatic Research Agents
2608.31076.paper_summary: Autonomous scientific research agents are increasingly applied to end-to-end scientific workflows, including literature review, data analysis, experimentation, and report generation. However, open-ended research tasks often do not clearly specify the analyses, methods, and success criteria required to complete the task. As a result, agents may miss important analyses, use inappropriate methods, or draw conclusions that are insufficiently supported by evidence. To address the problem, we present AutoSciRub, an evaluation-first framework that induces a task-specific executable rubric before research execution, and uses it to guide execution, criterion-level verification as well as iterative revision. AutoSciRub decomposes an underspecified instruction into atomic scientific goals, grounds them in relevant literature and task-visible data, and synthesizes specific, actionable, and verifiable criteria. The resulting rubric makes implicit experimental and evidential requirements explicit, providing guidance for experiments and analyses. During revision, rubric-guided verification identifies unmet criteria and enables targeted refinement of the research report and its supporting artifacts. On ResearchClawBench, AutoSciRub consistently improves all tested configurations, with an average gain of 2.08 points across three backbone LLMs under the fixed Codex harness and 2.95 points across three agent harnesses using a fixed DeepSeek-V4-Flash backbone. On a randomly sampled 20-task subset of AstaBench E2E Discovery, AutoSciRub further achieves an average improvement of 16.8 points across three agent harnesses, while maintaining or increasing the number of successfully completed tasks. These results demonstrate that evaluation-first guidance provides an effective and generalizable control mechanism for autonomous scientific research (Code: https://github.com/zjunlp/AutoSciRub).
2608.31076.paper_summary_zh: 自主科學研究代理越來越多地應用於端到端的科學工作流程，包括文獻回顧、數據分析、實驗和報告生成。<lb/>然而，開放式研究任務通常不會明確指定完成任務所需的分析、方法和成功標準。<lb/>因此，代理可能會錯過重要的分析、使用不當的方法，或得出證據支持不足的結論。<lb/>為了解決這個問題，我們提出了AutoSciRub，一個以評估為先的框架，在研究執行之前引入特定任務的可執行評分標準，並利用它來指導執行、標準級別的驗證以及迭代修訂。<lb/>AutoSciRub將不明確的指令分解為原子科學目標，並將它們基於相關文獻和可見數據進行基礎，合成具體、可行且可驗證的標準。<lb/>所生成的評分標準使隱含的實驗和證據要求變得明確，為實驗和分析提供指導。<lb/>在修訂過程中，基於評分標準的驗證識別未滿足的標準，並使研究報告及其支持材料的針對性改進成為可能。<lb/>在ResearchClawBench上，AutoSciRub始終改善所有測試配置，在固定的Codex工具下，三個基礎LLM的平均增益為2.08分，而在使用固定的DeepSeek-V4-Flash基礎的三個代理工具下，增益為2.95分。<lb/>在隨機抽樣的AstaBench E2E Discovery的20個任務子集上，AutoSciRub進一步在三個代理工具下實現了平均16.8分的改善，同時保持或增加成功完成的任務數量。<lb/>這些結果表明，以評估為先的指導提供了一種有效且可普遍應用的控制機制，用於自主科學研究（代碼：https://github.com/zjunlp/AutoSciRub）。
